newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels unite, want Berisha out.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels unite, want Berisha out.

text.p: South Albanian rebels have united in an umbrella group which called immediately for President Sali Berisha to resign, a rebel leader in this southern port said on Wednesday.

Xhvat Leeshi, an ex-army colonel and head of rebel-held Sarande, told a news conference that a number of rebel councils, stretching from Berat to Sarande, met on Tuesday and formed the National Committee for People's Salvation.
It was not clear whether the port of Vlore, which has struck a separate deal with the authorities, was included in the group.
Leeshi said the National Committee wanted a separate seat at all-party talks in Tirana which are trying to resolve the crisis in the Balkan country.
"We reiterated our demand for Berisha to resign. We want to be a separate body at the talks in Tirana," he said. The various rebel councils met in the southern town of Gjirokaster, he said.
An armed uprising has swept southern Albania over the past two weeks, with dozens of towns and villages being taken over by rebels opposing Berisha.
The crisis was triggered when popular investments schemes collapsed in January, wiping out the savings of thousands of Albanians.
Thousands of weapons have been looted from army arsenals over the past week, and the rebels in the southwest corner of Albania are now heavily armed, including artillery and tanks.

Gangs of armed men also roam the countryside uncontrolled and residents of all ages have joined in looting state property. An eight-storey hotel in Sarande was stripped clean on Tuesday and then set ablaze.
